subject: Post-demo: performance follow-up & token ceiling/streaming questions
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Novak <alex.novak@vectorlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: performance follow-up & token ceiling/streaming questions

Hi Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap and next steps from our end after the demo and perf discussion: 

Summary of requirements you articulated
- Latency: target p50 <= 80 ms, p95 <= 200 ms for interactive assistant flows (search+summarize).
- Throughput: sustained ~180–220 qps for discovery workload, occasional spikes to 400 qps for batch syncs.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent active sessions ~18–25; worst-case burst to ~50.
- Streaming: partial token streaming is required for the customer-facing UI to show progressive answers.
- Context: ~1.8k tokens of user input on average, peak input up to ~5k tokens (PDF ingestion + long context), expected output up to 1.5k tokens.

Immediate asks / open questions for us to qualify sizing and SLOs
- Can you confirm typical length distribution for the top 80% of requests (we heard ~600–2000 tokens)?
- For the PDF ingestion use-case, do you expect the entire 5k token payload to be sent on every request or as a cached/attachment reference?
- Streaming: is partial-turn streaming sufficient (i.e., stream hypotheses as they generate), or do you need token-level latency guarantees for first-byte (TTFB) under 50 ms?

Action items we’ll take this week
- Share a simple SLO matrix mapping context sizes to expected tail latency (attached: 2026-07-21_SLO-matrix.xlsx).
- Recommend an initial canary plan (Dedicated pool) and estimate unit cost delta for 8k vs 16k context ceilings.
- Marissa will follow up with a technical runbook and perf knobs we recommend for your traffic shape.

Attachments: 2026-07-21_SLO-matrix.xlsx (SLO-by-window-size spreadsheet)

Proposed next steps
- Marissa to propose canary config and perf validation tests (by Fri 24 Jul).
- Schedule a 60-min technical sync to finalize the canary gate criteria — suggested slot Tue 28 Jul 10:00 PT.

Thanks — I’ll loop in engineering if we need kernel-level optimizations, but for sizing we usually start with batching/quantization tradeoffs and streaming toggles.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Novak <alex.novak@vectorlytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@vectorlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:37:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance follow-up & token ceiling/streaming questions

Thanks Irene — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Token distributions
- Our telemetry shows 70% of requests are <= 1.2k tokens (input+expected output), 20% 1.2k–3k, and ~10% near the 5k peak you noted. I can export a histogram if helpful.

2) PDF ingestion
- For now, ingestion will be preprocessed and we will attach a compressed chunked representation for active sessions. Rarely will the full 5k be sent on every single request — mostly cached references, but we want the model to be able to attend across the full 5k window when needed.

3) Streaming needs
- Partial-turn streaming is sufficient for the UI. Our product team flagged that first-byte latency for starting the stream should be as low as possible — ideally under 100 ms p50, but we understand p95 will be higher with large contexts.

4) Environment preference
- We prefer starting on Dedicated capacity for the canary to mirror production network and GPU topology; we can evaluate Hosted afterward.

Can you include a back-of-envelope cost delta for supporting a 16k context ceiling vs an 8k ceiling for our expected traffic mix? Also happy to set up a short call to walk through the SLO matrix.

Cheers,
Alex Novak
CTO, VectorLytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>

Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance follow-up & token ceiling/streaming questions

Alex — thanks for the distro. A few concrete notes from the solutions engineering side (quick and actionable):

- Empirical latency impact by context ceiling (ballpark numbers on current gen A100-style profiles):
  * 8k ceiling: p50 ~ 50–70 ms, p95 ~ 140–220 ms for single-turn inference at 2–4k effective tokens (inference-only time, excludes network).
  * 16k ceiling: p50 + ~20–35 ms, p95 + ~80–140 ms on same token lengths due to attention scaling and KV cache pressure.

- Streaming behavior: enabling token-by-token streaming significantly improves perceived latency for users (first token is near-full-model latency for short contexts). For large contexts we recommend prefetching KV cache and using incremental decoding with chunked attention where possible. That yields better early-bird TTFB for the UI.

- Batching and concurrency: continuous batching will increase throughput but can add tail latency variance. For your target 180–220 qps with ~20 concurrent sessions, a small batching window (~20–30 ms) yields good utilization without pushing p95 beyond your target, assuming the model is quantized to int8 or int4.

- Cost tradeoffs: supporting 16k windows increases GPU memory footprint and may require moving from 40GB cards to 80GB cards for comfortable headroom; estimate ~1.6x–2x unit cost delta depending on quantization. We’ll produce a small cost matrix for your mix.

Attachments: redwood_perf_runbook_v1.pdf (recommended knobs and perf test plan)

Proposed canary criteria (suggested)
- Run 48-hour canary on Dedicated pool mirroring prod token mix (sampled): 70% <=1.2k, 20% 1.2–3k, 10% >3k.
- Verify p95 latency stays <= 200 ms for the interactive path with streaming enabled and batching window <=30 ms.
- Validate streaming TTFB p50 <= 100 ms.

If that looks good, we’ll draft the canary config and a Jenkins/GHA perf run with synthetic and recorded traffic. Happy to walk through results live.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

2) Commercials / paperwork- Irene will send a short amendment to the trial agreement covering Dedicated canary capacity and a refundable credit for the validation period. Expect a DocuSign link if you agree.
